claims.statement: UK remote-gambling guidance requires an ongoing process to identify harm, act to minimise it, record actions, evaluate effectiveness, and continue monitoring.

Remote operators and gambling-software licensees must comply with technical standards and testing procedures, creating a strong preference for auditable, integrator-distributed components rather than opaque standalone models.

Hypothesis: a player-account platform or approved test-house ecosystem can distribute one validated analytics layer to many operators, while pooled de-identified intervention outcomes improve indicator calibration faster than single-operator tools.

contrary_evidence: Operators already have customer-interaction systems, and guidance is outcome-oriented rather than prescribing a third-party model.
Supplying software into British remote gambling can itself trigger licensing and testing questions, increasing entry cost and legal complexity.

economics.acquisition_route: Win one platform or test partner through an offline benchmark, then reach multiple operators through that integration
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 20 platform or operator contracts averaging 300000 PLN ARR could reach 6 million PLN ARR in years 6-8; at 22% EBITDA, 6x EBITDA, and 70% ownership, founder equity could be about 5.5 million PLN, conditional on licensing and safety validation
economics.founder_time: 20-25 hours weekly through offline validation; live regulated deployment likely exceeds part-time capacity unless a platform funds implementation and compliance operations
economics.gross_margin_basis: Streaming inference can support 75-88% gross margin; validation, security, and compliance support are material costs
economics.payback: Target under 12 months per platform, justified by reusable compliance evidence and reduced manual review rather than revenue uplift
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 50000-250000 PLN annual platform licence plus usage tiers of 0.02-0.10 PLN per active account-day
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monitoring is continuous, models require drift review, and intervention evidence accumulates over the licence term

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned de-identified indicator-to-intervention outcomes, drift history, and audit mappings improve calibration and validation evidence
fingerprint.customer: Regulated remote gambling operators, player-account-management platforms, and compliance testing partners
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Integrated once into player-account platforms and distributed to their regulated operator portfolio
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Embedded interpretable risk-scoring, intervention ledger, and outcome-evaluation API with annual validation support
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Platform or operator pays by active-account tier and validated monitoring period
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A live player event stream must be monitored for harm indicators and every intervention must be recorded and evaluated

founder_fit: Strong data-science and domain-interest fit, with a platform distribution model and no consumer-facing persona. It is ethically and legally high-stakes, so the founder should use independent safer-gambling, privacy, and licensing oversight and restrict the initial product to offline evaluation on properly authorised data.
risks: False negatives can contribute to consumer harm, while false positives can unfairly restrict customers.
The product processes exceptionally sensitive behavioural and financial patterns and would face high security requirements.
A founder with a personal interest in gambling must manage conflicts and keep harm reduction, not engagement optimisation, as the binding product objective.

structure.control_point: The continuous harm-indicator, action, and evaluation ledger inside the operator's player-account system
structure.critical_dependency: A lawful software/licensing structure and access to representative event-and-intervention data for independent validation

thesis: Build a privacy-preserving behavioural-risk and intervention-evaluation layer that player-account-management platforms can embed for regulated remote gambling operators. It would ingest event streams, surface interpretable harm indicators, record actions, and measure whether interventions reduced risk; it would not set odds, accept bets, or make final account decisions.
title: SaferPlay Evidence API
uncertainties: Whether platform providers will share event data with a small external vendor is unknown.
Cross-operator model transfer may fail because game mix, customer base, and intervention policies differ.
The precise licensing perimeter for a risk-only component requires specialist counsel before any live deployment.
